end.summary:
Practised showing that consecutive odd numbers starting at 1 make square numbers.
Saanvi found totals 1+3+5+7+9=25 and the first seven odd numbers total 49.
Clarified that the run must start at 1; starting from 3 does not follow the same square pattern.
Practised combining consecutive triangular numbers to form a square; explained 10+15=25 as five equal rows of five dots.
Teach-back was not yet passed.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised using running totals and dot arrangements to connect odd-number sums and square numbers. They corrected the mix-up that any odd-number run makes a square: the pattern here starts with 1. They also explained how the 10-dot and 15-dot triangles combine into five rows of five dots. At home, ask them to draw the first four odd-number sums and label each resulting square.
